issues.description: Typo 'stlib' instead of 'stdlib' in the .. deprecated:: 4.3 docstring directive.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flagged this. The directive renders into Sphinx output and is the artifact users see when they hit the deprecation warning. Trivial fix, should be corrected before merge.

issues.description: Test only matches the tail of the deprecation warning and does not prove redirection still functions.
issues.detail: The pytest.warns pattern matches a substring of the suffix, so any prefix rewording passes silently. The test also does not establish that redirection (especially stderr and the restore-on-exception path) still behaves identically under the @deprecated wrapper. Tighten the match and cover the invariant.

issues.description: Deprecation message bundles redirect_stdout and redirect_stderr instead of presenting them as independent primitives.
issues.detail: Callers using only one redirection are told to use both. A one-line note that the two stdlib context managers are independent and composable would match the actual decomposition and make the substitution unambiguous.

synthesis.summary: Panel consensus: ACCEPT with trivial fixups. This is a well-scoped, single-purpose deprecation that replaces a bespoke context manager with two composable stdlib equivalents — the right direction, conservative staging (warn now, remove in 5.0), internal callers already migrated. Remaining issues are cosmetic and minor: a 'stlib' typo in the rendered Sphinx directive, a loose warning-message match in the new test that does not fully prove the redirection invariant, and a deprecation message that could better signal the two stdlib primitives are independent. Ship after the typo and message tidy.
